summary: Utah State needs clean possessions in Seattle. Watch the quarterback rotation, whether the offense protects the ball, and whether the secondary stays with its receivers when Washington’s quarterback extends a play.

items.headline: Hillstead remains the expected starter for Washington
items.tldr: Mendenhall said he anticipated Hillstead starting, and Monday’s depth chart kept him at QB1. Watch the opening series and how the staff uses Brosterhous’s planned weekly package.

items.headline: Williams added 61 rushing yards in Washington’s opener
items.tldr: Watch the pursuit angles as much as the initial pressure. If the quarterback extends a play, the secondary has to keep covering instead of chasing the scramble too soon.

items.headline: Four interceptions erased Utah State’s yardage advantage
items.tldr: Watch the decisions at the end of drives. A punt or a throwaway can leave the defense with a much better field than a forced pass.

items.headline: Washington is a 1:30 p.m. Mountain start on Big Ten Network
items.tldr: Check your channel access before kickoff. The official game guide gathers the broadcast, radio and live-stat links for the trip to Seattle.

items.headline: Wood led Utah State with six catches in the opener
items.tldr: Watch whether the offense can give its receivers catchable throws on schedule. Reliable completions would take pressure off both the run game and the defense.

lead.headline: Keep the next possession.
lead.body: Protect the ball, get lined up cleanly and make Washington earn the field. A promising drive only helps if the finish does not hand the advantage back.

matchup.question: What would make this a cleaner road performance?
matchup.answer: Avoid the forced throw on offense. On defense, keep the quarterback contained and stay on top of routes when the play lasts longer than expected.

signals.title: Quarterback usage
signals.detail: Watch how the staff divides the snaps and changes the package. A substitution alone is not enough to establish a permanent change at starter.

signals.title: Ball security
signals.detail: Watch the last decision of each possession. A throwaway can preserve field position when the coverage wins the play.
signals.prompt: How can Utah State protect its possessions?

signals.title: Containment
signals.detail: Watch whether the secondary stays with its receivers when the quarterback moves. Pursuit cannot leave a free throw behind it.
signals.prompt: How should Utah State defend Washington’s quarterback?

signals.title: Receiving rhythm
signals.detail: Watch whether the passing game finds a catchable ball before the pocket breaks down. Consistent completions can keep the offense out of long-yardage situations.
signals.prompt: What should I watch in Utah State’s passing game?
